ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a series of triangular patterns is shown from left to right. The 1st large triangle has no shading inside; each side of the 2nd triangle is divided into 2 equal parts, and there is 1 inverted small triangle inside that is shaded black; each side of the 3rd triangle is divided into 3 equal parts, and 3 inverted small triangles are shaded black; each side of the 4th triangle is divided into 4 equal parts, and 6 inverted small triangles are shaded black, arranged as 1+2+3. Reasoning: According to the pattern, each side of the nth triangle is divided into n equal parts, so the inside can be regarded as being composed of n^2 small triangles of equal area. The numbers of shaded inverted small triangles are successively 0, 1, 3, 6, corresponding to the nth one being 1+2+...+(n-1)=n(n-1)/2. The number of shaded triangles in the 8th triangle is 8×7/2=28, and the total number of small-triangle area units is 8^2=64, so the shaded part accounts for 28/64=7/16.
